title.zh: 卷二十五 志第十五 曆一
title.raw: 卷二十五 志第十五 曆一 Volume 25 Treatises 16: Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 曆法尚矣。

translations.literal: Calendar methods are of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: The art of calendrics has been esteemed since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自堯命羲、和，曆象日月星辰，以閏月定四時成歲，其事略見於《書》。

translations.literal: From Yao's command to Xi and He to regulate the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, using intercalary months to fix the four seasons and complete the year—the matter is briefly seen in the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao charged Xi and He to observe the heavens and set the calendar by intercalary months, fixing the seasons and the year, the gist appears in the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 而夏、商、周以三統改正朔，為曆固已不同，而其法不傳。

translations.literal: Yet Xia, Shang, and Zhou each revised the calendar beginning through the Three Conformities, so the calendars were already different, while their methods were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xia, Shang, and Zhou each adjusted the new-year reckoning by the Three Conformities system, so their calendars already diverged, but none of those methods survive.

sentences.zh: 至漢造曆，始以八十一分為統母，其數起于黃鐘之龠，蓋其法一本於律矣。

translations.literal: By Han times in making calendars, they first took eighty-one parts as the conformity mother; the number arose from the Yellow Bell pitch-pipe, for the method was fundamentally based on pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han first devised a calendar, they took eighty-one as the mother of conformity, deriving the figure from the Yellow Bell tube—calendrics rooted in musical pitch.

sentences.zh: 其後劉歆又以《春秋》、《易象》推合其數，蓋傅會之說也。

translations.literal: Later Liu Xin again used the Spring and Autumn Annals and Changes imagery to align the numbers—largely forced correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin later forced the numbers to agree with the Spring and Autumn and the Book of Changes—a contrived harmonization.

sentences.zh: 至唐一行始專用大衍之策，則曆術又本于《易》矣。

translations.literal: By Tang times Yixing alone devoted himself to the Dayan procedures, and calendrical technique was again based on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, the monk Yixing relied chiefly on the Great Expansion methods, so calendrical science again took the Changes as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 蓋曆起於數，數者，自然之用也。

translations.literal: For calendars arise from number; number is nature's instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Calendars begin in number, and number is the working tool of the natural order.

sentences.zh: 其用無窮而無所不通，以之于律、于《易》，皆可以合也。

translations.literal: Its use is inexhaustible and nothing is impenetrable; applied to pitch standards or to the Changes, all can be made to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Number's applications are boundless; whether joined to musical pitch or to the Changes, everything can be fitted together.

sentences.zh: 然其要在於候天地之氣，以知四時寒暑，而仰察天日月星之行運，以相參合而已。

translations.literal: Yet the essence lies in awaiting heaven-and-earth's qi to know the four seasons' cold and heat, and looking up to observe sun, moon, and stars' motion to compare and harmonize—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The heart of the matter is to read seasonal qi on earth and compare it with the observed courses of sun, moon, and stars in the sky.

sentences.zh: 然四時寒暑無形而運于下，天日月星有象而見於上，二者常動而不息。

translations.literal: Yet the four seasons' cold and heat are formless and operate below; heaven's sun, moon, and stars have form and appear above—the two are ever in motion without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal warmth and cold move invisibly on earth, while the luminaries show visible patterns above; both realms move ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 一有一無，出入升降，或遲或疾，不相為謀。

translations.literal: One present, one absent; entering and leaving, rising and falling, now slow, now swift—they do not consult one another.
translations.idiomatic: They alternate presence and absence, rise and fall, speed up and slow down, without any mutual agreement.

sentences.zh: 其久而不能無差忒者，勢使之然也。

translations.literal: That over long time there cannot be without discrepancy is what circumstance makes inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Given enough time, error is inevitable—that is the nature of the case.

sentences.zh: 故為曆者，其始未嘗不精密，而其後多疏而不合，亦理之然也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who make calendars at first are never not precise, yet later mostly become loose and fail to agree—this too is reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: New calendars start precise, then drift out of alignment; that pattern is itself predictable.

sentences.zh: 不合，則屢變其法以求之。

translations.literal: When they fail to agree, they repeatedly change the method to seek agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When predictions fail, reformers revise the rules again and again.

sentences.zh: 自堯、舜、三代以來，曆未嘗同也。

translations.literal: From Yao and Shun through the Three Dynasties, calendars have never been the same.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties, no two reigns have kept the same calendar.

sentences.zh: 唐終始二百九十餘年，而曆八改。

translations.literal: Tang from beginning to end was somewhat more than two hundred ninety years, yet the calendar was changed eight times.
translations.idiomatic: Across Tang's roughly two hundred ninety years, the official calendar was replaced eight times.

sentences.zh: 初曰《戊寅元曆》，曰《麟德甲子元曆》，曰《開元大衍曆》，曰《寶應五紀曆》，曰《建中正元曆》，曰《元和觀象曆》，曰《長慶宣明曆》，曰《景福崇玄曆》而止矣。

translations.literal: First called the Wuyin Origin Calendar, then the Lindé Jiazi Origin Calendar, the Kaiyuan Dayan Calendar, the Baoying Five Reckonings Calendar, the Jianzhong Zhengyuan Calendar, the Yuanhe Guanxiang Calendar, the Changqing Xuanming Calendar, ending with the Jingfu Chongxuan Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In order: the Wuyin Origin, Lindé Jiazi Origin, Kaiyuan Dayan, Baoying Five Reckonings, Jianzhong Zhengyuan, Yuanhe Guanxiang, Changqing Xuanming, and finally the Jingfu Chongxuan calendars.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，將治新曆，東都道士傅仁均善推步之學，太史令庾儉、丞傅弈薦之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, about to regulate a new calendar, the Eastern Capital Daoist Fu Renjun was skilled in progression-and-step astronomy; Grand Astrologer Yu Jian and Vice-Director Fu Yi recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne he planned a new calendar; the Daoist Fu Renjun of the eastern capital, expert in astronomical computation, was recommended by Yu Jian and Fu Yi.

sentences.zh: 詔仁均與儉等參議，合受命歲名為《戊寅元曆》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Renjun with Jian and others to deliberate jointly, naming the calendar after the year of receiving the mandate: the Wuyin Origin Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Renjun worked with Yu Jian and others and named the system the Wuyin Origin Calendar after Tang's inaugural year.

sentences.zh: 乃列其大要，所可考驗者有七，曰：「唐以戊寅歲甲子日登極，曆元戊寅，日起甲子，如漢《太初》，一也。

translations.literal: He then listed the main points; seven matters could be tested, saying: "Tang on the wuyin year's jiazi day ascended the throne; calendar origin wuyin, days beginning jiazi, like Han Taichu—first."
translations.idiomatic: Renjun set out seven verifiable claims: Tang enthroned on jiazi day in a wuyin year, with wuyin as calendar origin and days counted from jiazi—as in Han Taichu (point one).

sentences.zh: 冬至五十餘年輒差一度，日短星昴，合於《堯典》，二也。

translations.literal: Winter solstice every fifty-odd years then differs by one degree; days short and stars at Mao—agreeing with the Canon of Yao—second.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice shifts one degree every fifty-some years; short days with Mao culminating matches the Yao canon (point two).

sentences.zh: 周幽王六年十月辛卯朔，入蝕限，合於《詩》，三也。

translations.literal: King You of Zhou year six, tenth month xinmao new moon, entering eclipse limits—agreeing with the Odes—third.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou King You's sixth year, tenth month xinmao new moon within eclipse limits, matches the Odes (point three).

sentences.zh: 魯僖公五年壬子冬至，合《春秋命曆序》，四也。

translations.literal: Duke Xi of Lu year five renzi winter solstice—agreeing with Spring and Autumn Calendar Order—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duke Xi's fifth year renzi winter solstice agrees with the Spring and Autumn calendar sequence (point four).

sentences.zh: 月有三大、三小，則日蝕常在朔，月蝕常在望，五也。

translations.literal: Months with three long and three short, then solar eclipses always at new moon, lunar eclipses always at full moon—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Three long and three short months place solar eclipses at new moon and lunar eclipses at full moon (point five).

sentences.zh: 命辰起子半，命度起虛六，符陰陽之始，六也。

translations.literal: Naming the double-hour from zi half, naming degrees from Xu six—matching yin-yang's beginning—sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Hours reckoned from mid-zi, degrees from Xu 6, aligning yin-yang origins (point six).

sentences.zh: 立遲疾定朔，則月行晦不東見，朔不西朓，七也。

translations.literal: Establishing slow-fast to fix new moon, then at month end the moon is not seen in the east, at new moon not thin in the west—seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Slow-fast tables for true new moon keep the moon invisible in the east at month-end and not a western sliver at new moon (point seven).

sentences.zh: 」高祖詔司曆起二年用之，擢仁均員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: " Gaozu ordered the calendar office to use it from year two, promoting Renjun to Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered adoption from year two and made Renjun Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三年正月望及二月、八月朔，當蝕，比不效。

translations.literal: Year three first-month full moon and second and eighth months' new moons, when eclipses were due, in comparison did not match.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, predicted eclipses at the first-month full moon and at second- and eighth-month new moons failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔吏部郎中祖孝孫考其得失。

translations.literal: Year six, an edict ordered Ministry of Personnel Director Zu Xiaosun to examine its gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, Zu Xiaosun of the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to review the calendar's errors.

sentences.zh: 孝孫使算曆博士王孝通以《甲辰曆》法詰之曰：「'日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: Xiaosun had Calendar Computation Doctor Wang Xiaotong use the Jiachen Calendar method to challenge him, saying: "'Days short, stars at Mao—to rectify mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun had Wang Xiaotong challenge him with the Jiachen Calendar: "'Days short, stars at Mao' fixes mid-winter."

sentences.zh: '七宿畢見，舉中宿言耳。

translations.literal: ' The seven lodges all appear—speaking of the culminating lodge only.
translations.idiomatic: When all seven lodges are visible, the text names only the one at culmination.

sentences.zh: 舉中宿，則餘星可知。

translations.literal: Naming the culminating lodge, then the rest of the stars can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Name the culminating lodge and the rest follow.

sentences.zh: 仁均專守昴中，執文害意，不亦謬乎？

translations.literal: Renjun alone holds Mao at culmination, clinging to the text and harming the meaning—is it not absurd?
translations.idiomatic: Renjun insists only on Mao at culmination, slave to the letter—is that not wrong?

sentences.zh: 又《月令》仲冬'昏東壁中'，明昴中非為常准。

translations.literal: Again the Monthly Ordinances mid-winter 'evening Wall at culmination' shows Mao at culmination is not the constant standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances place Wall at culmination in mid-winter, so Mao is not the fixed norm.

sentences.zh: 若堯時星昴昏中，差至東壁，然則堯前七千餘歲，冬至昏翼中，日應在東井。

translations.literal: If at Yao's time stars Mao at evening culmination, the offset reaching Wall, then before Yao by seven thousand-odd years winter solstice evening would have Wings at culmination and the sun should be at Well.
translations.idiomatic: If Yao had Mao culminating at winter solstice, extrapolating back seven thousand years puts Wings culminating and the sun at Well.

sentences.zh: 井極北，去人最近，故暑；

translations.literal: Well is utmost north, nearest people, hence heat;
translations.idiomatic: Well lies far north and nearest the observer, hence summer heat;

sentences.zh: 斗極南，去人最遠，故寒。

translations.literal: Dipper is utmost south, farthest from people, hence cold.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper lies far south and farthest away, hence winter cold.

sentences.zh: 寒暑易位，必不然矣。

translations.literal: Cold and heat exchanging places—surely it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Swapping summer and winter seasons—that cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 又平朔、定朔，舊有二家。

translations.literal: Again mean new moon and true new moon—of old there were two schools.
translations.idiomatic: Mean versus true new moon had long been two rival methods.

sentences.zh: 三大、三小，為定朔望；

translations.literal: Three long and three short—for true new and full moon;
translations.idiomatic: Three long and three short months belong to true conjunction reckoning;

sentences.zh: 一大、一小，為平朔望。

translations.literal: one long and one short—for mean new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: one long and one short to mean conjunction reckoning.

sentences.zh: 日月行有遲速，相及謂之合會。

translations.literal: Sun and moon motion have slow and swift; when they reach each other it is called conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon move unevenly; their meeting is conjunction.

sentences.zh: 晦、朔無定，由時消息。

translations.literal: Month-end and new moon are not fixed, following the seasons' wax and wane.
translations.idiomatic: Last day and new moon shift with seasonal irregularities.

sentences.zh: 若定大小皆在朔者，合會雖定，而蔀、元、紀首三端並失。

translations.literal: If fixing long and short all at new moon, though conjunction is fixed, the three origins of obscuration, era, and cycle-head are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing every long/short month to new moon fixes conjunction but breaks obscuration, era, and cycle-head alignment.

sentences.zh: 若上合履端之始，下得歸餘於終，合會有時，則《甲辰元曆》為通術矣。

translations.literal: If above it meets the year's beginning and below returns remainder at the end, conjunction occurring in season, then the Jiachen Origin Calendar is the comprehensive method.
translations.idiomatic: If cycle-heads align at the year start and remainders at year end, the Jiachen Origin Calendar is the sound general method.

sentences.zh: 」仁均對曰：「宋祖沖之立歲差，隋張胄玄等因而修之。

translations.literal: " Renjun replied: "Song's Zu Chongzhi established precession; Sui's Zhang Zexuan and others revised it thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Renjun answered: Zu Chongzhi of Liu-Song founded precession; Zhang Zexuan of Sui and others refined it.

sentences.zh: 雖差數不同，各明其意。

translations.literal: Though the difference numbers differ, each clarified his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Their constants differed, but each school knew its own aim.

sentences.zh: 孝通未曉，乃熱南斗為冬至常星。

translations.literal: Xiaotong did not understand, yet insisted Dipper was the winter-solstice constant star.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong missed the point and still treated Dipper as the fixed winter-solstice star.

sentences.zh: 夫日躔宿度，如垂阝傳之過，宿度既差，黃道隨而變矣。

translations.literal: The sun's lodge crossing is like a gnomon's passage; once lodge degrees shift, the yellow path shifts with them.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's motion through lodges shifts like a gnomon shadow; lodge drift moves the ecliptic too.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：'季秋月朔，辰弗集于房。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'Last month of autumn, new moon, the chronogram not gathered at Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents record: 'Autumn's last month, new moon—the chronogram not assembled at Fang.'

sentences.zh: '孔氏云：'集，合也。

translations.literal: ' Kong's commentary: 'Gathered means united.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yingda: 'Gathered means in conjunction.'

sentences.zh: 不合則日蝕可知。

translations.literal: Not united then solar eclipse can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If not united, a solar eclipse is implied.

sentences.zh: '又云：'先時者殺無赦，不及時者殺無赦。

translations.literal: ' Again: 'Those before the time kill without pardon; those after the time kill without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Too early—execute without mercy; too late—execute without mercy.'

sentences.zh: '既有先後之差，是知定朔矣。

translations.literal: ' Since there is before-and-after discrepancy, this shows true new moon.
translations.idiomatic: That timing error proves true new moon reckoning.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'十月之交，朔月辛卯。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'At the tenth month's junction, new moon xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes: 'At the tenth month's turn, new moon on xinmao.'

sentences.zh: '又《春秋傳》曰：'不書朔，官失之也。

translations.literal: ' Again the Zuo Commentary: 'Not recording new moon—the office failed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: 'Failure to record new moon was the clerks' fault.'

sentences.zh: '自後曆差，莫能詳正。

translations.literal: ' Since later calendars erred, none could correct in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Later calendars drifted and no one could fix them fully.

sentences.zh: 故秦、漢以來，多非朔蝕。

translations.literal: Therefore from Qin and Han onward, many eclipses were not at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Qin and Han records often place eclipses off new moon.

sentences.zh: 宋御史中丞何承天微欲見意，不能詳究，乃為散騎侍郎皮延宗等所抑。

translations.literal: Song Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian faintly wished to show the idea but could not investigate in detail, and was suppressed by Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Pi Yanzong and others.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of Song glimpsed the idea but could not finish; Pi Yanzong and others blocked him.

sentences.zh: 孝通之語，乃延宗舊說。

translations.literal: Xiaotong's words are Yanzong's old doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong merely repeated Yanzong's old argument.

sentences.zh: 治曆之本，必推上元，日月如合璧，五星如連珠，夜半甲子朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: The root of regulating calendars must push the high origin: sun and moon like joined jades, five stars like strung pearls, midnight jiazi new-moon dawn winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-making must reckon a high origin when sun and moon conjoin and the five planets align at midnight jiazi on winter-solstice new moon.

sentences.zh: 自此七曜散行，不復餘分普盡，總會如初。

translations.literal: From this the seven luminaries scatter; remainder parts do not all exhaust; the grand conjunction returns as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the seven wanderers diverge until remainders cycle and all align again.

sentences.zh: 唯朔分、氣分，有可盡之理，因其可盡，即有三端。

translations.literal: Only new-moon parts and qi parts have exhaustible principle; because they can exhaust, there are three origins.
translations.idiomatic: Only new-moon and qi fractions can fully cycle; that exhaustibility yields the three origins.

sentences.zh: 此乃紀其日數之元爾。

translations.literal: This merely records the origin of day-counts.
translations.idiomatic: That is simply the epoch for counting days.

sentences.zh: 或以為即夜半甲子朔冬至者，非也。

translations.literal: Some think it is exactly midnight jiazi new-moon winter solstice—not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some equate the three origins with midnight jiazi winter-solstice new moon—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 冬至自有常數，朔名由於月起，月行遲疾匪常，三端安得即合。

translations.literal: Winter solstice has its own constant; the name new moon arises from the moon's beginning; the moon's slow-fast is not constant—how can the three origins coincide at once?
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice is regular; new moon follows the moon; lunar speed varies—the three origins cannot coincide by definition.

sentences.zh: 故必須日月相合與至同日者，乃為合朔冬至耳。

translations.literal: Therefore sun and moon must conjoin on the same day as the solstice—only then is it conjoined new-moon winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: True epoch new-moon winter solstice requires sun and moon to conjoin on the solstice day itself.

sentences.zh: 」孝孫以為然，但略去尤疏闊者。

translations.literal: " Xiaosun agreed, but only removed the most gross errors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun accepted this, trimming only the worst flaws.

sentences.zh: 九年，復詔大理卿崔善為與孝通等較定，善為所改凡數十條。

translations.literal: Year nine, again an edict ordered Chief Minister of Justice Cui Shanyi with Xiaotong and others to compare and fix; Shanyi's changes numbered several tens of items.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, Cui Shanyi and Xiaotong revised dozens of rules.

sentences.zh: 初，仁均以武德元年為曆始，而氣、朔、遲疾、交會及五星皆有加減。

translations.literal: At first Renjun took Wude year one as calendar beginning, while qi, new moon, slow-fast, conjunction, and five stars all had additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Renjun had begun from Wude year one with adjustments to qi, new moons, lunar speed, nodes, and planets.

sentences.zh: 至是復用上元積算。

translations.literal: By now they again used high-origin accumulated computation.
translations.idiomatic: Now they reverted to high-origin accumulated counts.

sentences.zh: 其周天度，即古赤道也。

translations.literal: Its circuit-of-heaven degrees are the ancient equator.
translations.idiomatic: Its celestial circuit degrees follow the old equator.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，直太史李淳風又上疏論十有八事，復詔善為課二家得失，其七條改從淳風。

translations.literal: Early Zhenguan, Attendant Grand Astrologer Li Chunfeng again memorialized discussing eighteen matters; again an edict ordered Shanyi to grade the two schools' gains and losses—seven items changed to follow Chunfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhenguan, Li Chunfeng petitioned on eighteen points; seven revisions followed his method after Shanyi compared both schools.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太宗將親祀南郊，以十一月癸亥朔，甲子冬至。

translations.literal: Year fourteen, Taizong was to sacrifice at the southern suburb on eleventh month guihai new moon, jiazi winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen Taizong would sacrifice at the southern altar when guihai new moon and jiazi winter solstice fell in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 而淳風新術，以甲子合朔冬至，乃上言：「古曆分日，起於子半。

translations.literal: Chunfeng's new method had jiazi conjoined new moon at winter solstice, so he submitted: "Ancient calendars divided the day from zi half.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng's new astronomy placed jiazi new moon on winter solstice and argued days should begin at mid-zi.

sentences.zh: 十一月當甲子合朔冬至，故太史令傅仁均以減餘稍多，子初為朔，遂差三刻。

translations.literal: Eleventh month should have jiazi conjoined new moon winter solstice; therefore Grand Astrologer Fu Renjun, subtracting remainder slightly too much, made zi beginning the new moon, thus differing by three quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Renjun's excess subtraction made new moon fall at zi start, missing the solstice by three quarters.

sentences.zh: 」司曆南宮子明、太史令薛頤等言：「子初及半，日月未離。

translations.literal: " Calendar officers Nangong Ziming, Grand Astrologer Xue Yi, and others said: "At zi beginning and half, sun and moon had not separated.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming and Xue Yi replied that at zi start the luminaries had not yet separated.

sentences.zh: 淳風之法，較春秋已來晷度薄蝕，事皆符合。

translations.idiomatic: From entering Minor Snow through Major Snow, uniformly subtract 8 days.

sentences.zh: 初見，順，日行百七十一分，日益遲一分，百一十四日行十九度二百九分。

translations.literal: First appearance: direct motion, daily 171 parts, daily one part slower, in 114 days travels 19 degrees 209 parts.
translations.idiomatic: At first appearance it moves directly, 171 parts per day, slowing by 1 part each day; in 114 days it travels 19 degrees 209 parts.

sentences.zh: 而留，二十六日。

translations.literal: Then it stations for 26 days.
translations.idiomatic: Then it stations for 26 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退，日九十七分，八十四日退十二度三十六分。

translations.literal: Then retrograde: daily 97 parts; in 84 days retreats 12 degrees 36 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then it retrogrades 97 parts per day; in 84 days it retreats 12 degrees 36 parts.

sentences.zh: 又留，二十五日五百九十六分，小分七。

translations.literal: Again it stations for 25 days 596 parts, minor parts 7.
translations.idiomatic: Again it stations for 25 days 596 parts, minor parts 7.

sentences.zh: 凡五星留日有分者，以初定見日分加之。

translations.literal: For all five planets, when stationary days have parts, add the parts of the first fixed appearance day.
translations.idiomatic: For all five planets, when stationary days carry fractional parts, add the parts from the first fixed appearance day.

sentences.zh: 若滿行分法，去之，又增一日。

translations.literal: If they fill the motion-parts factor, remove and add one day.
translations.idiomatic: If they fill the motion-parts factor, cast out the excess and add one day.

sentences.zh: 乃順，初日行六十分，日益疾一分，百一十四日行十九度四百三十七分。

translations.literal: Then direct: first day 60 parts, daily one part faster, in 114 days travels 19 degrees 437 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then it moves directly again: 60 parts on the first day, speeding by 1 part each day; in 114 days it travels 19 degrees 437 parts.

sentences.zh: 而伏。

translations.literal: Then concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Then it becomes invisible.

sentences.zh: 率七百三十八萬一千二百二十三。

translations.idiomatic: Sidereal rate: 7,381,223.

sentences.zh: 終日七百七十九，行分六百二十六，小分三。

translations.literal: Total days 779, motion parts 626, minor parts 3.
translations.idiomatic: Total days: 779; motion parts: 626; minor parts: 3.

sentences.zh: 平見，入冬至初日，減萬六千三百五十四分。

translations.literal: At mean appearance, on the first day after entering winter solstice, subtract 16,354 parts.
translations.idiomatic: At mean appearance, on the first day after entering winter solstice, subtract 16,354 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃日損所減五百四十五分。

translations.literal: Then daily decrease the amount subtracted by 545 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease the subtracted amount by 545 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 入大寒，日增所加四百二十六分。

translations.literal: Upon entering Major Cold, daily increase the amount added by 426 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering Major Cold, increase the added amount by 426 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 入雨水後，均加二十九日。

translations.literal: After entering Rain Water, uniformly add 29 days.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Rain Water, uniformly add 29 days.

sentences.zh: 立夏初日，加萬九千三百九十二分。

translations.literal: On the first day of Establishment of Summer, add 19,392 parts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of Establishment of Summer, add 19,392 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃日損所加二百一十三分。

translations.literal: Then daily decrease the amount added by 213 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease the added amount by 213 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 入立秋初，依平。

translations.literal: Upon entering the first day of Establishment of Autumn, follow the mean rate.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the first day of Establishment of Autumn, follow the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 入處暑，日增所減百八十四分。

translations.literal: Upon entering End of Heat, daily increase the amount subtracted by 184 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering End of Heat, increase the subtracted amount by 184 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 入小雪後，均減二十五日。

translations.literal: After entering Minor Snow, uniformly subtract 25 days.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Minor Snow, uniformly subtract 25 days.

sentences.zh: 初見，入冬至，初率二百四十一日行百六十三度。

translations.literal: First appearance, upon entering winter solstice: initial rate 241 days travels 163 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At first appearance upon entering winter solstice, the initial rate is 241 days for 163 degrees of travel.

sentences.zh: 自後二日損日度各一，自百二十八日，率百七十七日行九十九度，畢百六十一日。

translations.literal: Afterward every 2 days decrease day and degree each by 1; from day 128, rate 177 days travels 99 degrees, completing 161 days.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter decrease the day-rate and degree-rate by 1 every 2 days; from day 128 the rate is 177 days for 99 degrees, completing 161 days.

sentences.zh: 又三日損一，盡百八十二日，率百七十日行九十二度，畢百八十八日。

translations.literal: Again every 3 days decrease by 1; through 182 days, rate 170 days travels 92 degrees, completing 188 days.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease by 1 every 3 days; through 182 days the rate is 170 days for 92 degrees, completing 188 days.

sentences.zh: 乃三日益一，盡二百二十七日，率百八十三日行百五度。

translations.literal: Then every 3 days increase by 1; through 227 days, rate 183 days travels 105 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 every 3 days; through 227 days the rate is 183 days for 105 degrees.

sentences.zh: 又二日益一，盡二百四十九日，率百九十四日行百一十六度。

translations.literal: Again every 2 days increase by 1; through 249 days, rate 194 days travels 116 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 every 2 days; through 249 days the rate is 194 days for 116 degrees.

sentences.zh: 又每日益一，盡二百一十日，率二百五十五日行百七十七度，畢三百三十七日。

translations.literal: Again daily increase by 1; through 210 days, rate 255 days travels 177 degrees, completing 337 days.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 each day; through 210 days the rate is 255 days for 177 degrees, completing 337 days.

sentences.zh: 乃二日損一，盡大雪，復初見。

translations.literal: Then every 2 days decrease by 1; through Major Snow, return to first appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease by 1 every 2 days; through Major Snow it returns to first appearance.

sentences.zh: 入小寒後，三日去日率一。

translations.literal: After entering Minor Cold, every 3 days remove 1 from the day-rate.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Minor Cold, remove 1 from the day-rate every 3 days.

sentences.zh: 入雨水，畢立夏，均去日率二十。

translations.literal: From entering Rain Water through Establishment of Summer, uniformly remove 20 from the day-rate.
translations.idiomatic: From entering Rain Water through Establishment of Summer, uniformly remove 20 from the day-rate.

sentences.zh: 自後三日減所去一日，畢小暑，依平，為定日率。

translations.literal: Afterward every 3 days decrease the removed amount by 1 day; through Minor Heat, follow the mean rate—that is the fixed day-rate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter decrease the removed amount by 1 day every 3 days; through Minor Heat follow the mean rate—this is the fixed day-rate.

sentences.zh: 若入處暑，畢秋分，皆去度率六。

translations.literal: If entering End Heat through Autumn Equinox, all remove six from the degree-rate.
translations.idiomatic: If the motion begins between End Heat and Autumn Equinox, subtract 6 from the degree-rate throughout.

sentences.zh: 各依冬至後日數而損益之，又依所入之氣以減之，為前疾日度率。

translations.literal: Each according to days after winter solstice increase or decrease them, also according to the qi entered subtract from them, as the day-rate and degree-rate for initial rapid.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust each according to the number of days past the winter solstice and subtract according to the solar term entered, to obtain the day-rate and degree-rate for the initial rapid phase.

sentences.zh: 若初行入大寒，畢大暑，皆差行，日益遲一分；

translations.literal: If initial motion enters Great Cold through Great Heat, all differential motion, each day increasingly slower by one part;
translations.idiomatic: If the initial motion falls between Great Cold and Great Heat, use variable motion, slowing by 1 part each day;

sentences.zh: 其餘皆平行。

translations.literal: The rest all uniform motion.
translations.idiomatic: In all other seasons, use uniform motion.

sentences.zh: 若入白露，畢秋分，初遲，日行半度，四十日行二十度。

translations.literal: If entering White Dew through Autumn Equinox, initial slow, daily motion half a degree, in forty days motion twenty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If entering between White Dew and Autumn Equinox, start with slow motion at half a degree per day, covering 20 degrees in 40 days.

sentences.zh: 即去日率四十、度率二十，別為半度之。

translations.literal: Then remove forty from day-rate and twenty from degree-rate, separately treat as half-degree motion.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside 40 days of the day-rate and 20 degrees of the degree-rate as a separate half-degree segment.

sentences.zh: 行訖，然後求平行分，續之。

translations.literal: When motion is finished, then seek the uniform-motion parts and continue.
translations.idiomatic: When that segment is complete, calculate the uniform-motion parts and continue from there.

sentences.zh: 以行分法乘度定率，如日定率而一，為平行分。

translations.literal: Multiply the fixed degree-rate by the motion-parts factor, divide by the fixed day-rate as one, as uniform-motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fixed degree-rate by the motion-parts factor and divide by the fixed day-rate to get the uniform-motion parts.

sentences.zh: 不盡，為小分。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust is minor parts.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder gives the minor parts.

sentences.zh: 求差行者，減日率一，又半之，加平行分，為初日行分。

translations.literal: Seeking differential motion, subtract one from day-rate, again halve it, add uniform-motion parts, as initial day motion-parts.
translations.idiomatic: For differential motion, subtract 1 from the day-rate, halve the result, add to the uniform-motion parts—that yields the initial day's motion-parts.

sentences.zh: 各盡其日度而遲。

translations.literal: Each exhausts its days and degrees, then slow.
translations.idiomatic: Continue until the allotted days and degrees are used up, then enter slow motion.

sentences.zh: 初日行三百二十六分，日益遲一分半，六十日行二十五度五分。

translations.literal: Initial day motion three hundred twenty-six parts, each day increasingly slower one and a half parts, in sixty days motion twenty-five degrees five parts.
translations.idiomatic: Initial daily motion is 326 parts, slowing by 1.5 parts each day; in 60 days it covers 25 degrees and 5 parts.

sentences.zh: 其前疾去度六者，行三十一度五分。

translations.literal: If the initial rapid removed six from degrees, motion thirty-one degrees five parts.
translations.idiomatic: If the initial rapid phase had 6 degrees subtracted, the distance covered is 31 degrees and 5 parts.

sentences.zh: 此遲初日加六十七分、小分六十分之三十六。

translations.literal: This slow phase initial day add sixty-seven parts, minor parts thirty-six sixtieths.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of this slow phase add 67 parts and 36/60 minor parts.

sentences.zh: 而留，十三日。

translations.literal: Then stationary, thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Then it stands still for 13 days.

sentences.zh: 前疾去日者，分日於二留，奇從後留。

translations.literal: If initial rapid removed days, divide days between the two stations, remainder follows the later station.
translations.idiomatic: If days were subtracted during initial rapid motion, split those days between the two stationary periods, with any odd days assigned to the later one.

sentences.zh: 乃退，日百九十二分，六十日退十七度二十八分。

translations.literal: Then retrograde, daily one hundred ninety-two parts, in sixty days retrograde seventeen degrees twenty-eight parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then it retrogrades at 192 parts per day, covering 17 degrees 28 parts in 60 days.

sentences.zh: 又留，十二日六百二十六分，小分三。

translations.literal: Again stationary, twelve days six hundred twenty-six parts, minor parts three.
translations.idiomatic: It stands still again for 12 days 626 parts, 3 minor parts.

sentences.zh: 又順。

translations.literal: Again direct.
translations.idiomatic: Then it resumes direct motion.

sentences.zh: 後遲，初日行二百三十八分，日益疾一分半，六十日行二十五度三十五分。

translations.literal: Later slow, initial day motion two hundred thirty-eight parts, each day increasingly faster one and a half parts, in sixty days motion twenty-five degrees thirty-five parts.
translations.idiomatic: In the later slow phase, initial daily motion is 238 parts, accelerating by 1.5 parts each day; in 60 days it covers 25 degrees 35 parts.

sentences.zh: 此遲在立秋至秋分者，加六度，行三十一度三十五分。

translations.literal: If this slow phase is from Start of Autumn through Autumn Equinox, add six degrees, motion thirty-one degrees thirty-five parts.
translations.idiomatic: If this slow phase falls between Start of Autumn and Autumn Equinox, add 6 degrees—for a total of 31 degrees 35 parts.

sentences.zh: 此遲初日加行分六十七、小分六十分之三十六。

translations.literal: This slow initial day add motion-parts sixty-seven, minor parts thirty-six sixtieths.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of this slow phase, add 67 motion-parts and 36/60 minor parts.

sentences.zh: 而後疾。

translations.literal: Then later rapid.
translations.idiomatic: Then comes the later rapid phase.

sentences.zh: 入冬至，初率二百一十四日行百三十六度。

translations.literal: Entering winter solstice, initial rate two hundred fourteen days motion one hundred thirty-six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Entering winter solstice, the initial rate is 136 degrees in 214 days.

sentences.zh: 乃每日損一，盡三十七日，率百七十七日行九十九度。

translations.literal: Then each day diminish by one, exhaust thirty-seven days, rate one hundred seventy-seven days motion ninety-nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease by 1 each day for 37 days, yielding a rate of 99 degrees in 177 days.

sentences.zh: 又二日損一，盡五十七日，率百六十七日行八十九度，畢七十九日。

translations.literal: Again every two days diminish by one, exhaust fifty-seven days, rate one hundred sixty-seven days motion eighty-nine degrees, exhaust seventy-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Next, decrease by 1 every 2 days for 57 days, giving 89 degrees in 167 days—a segment of 79 days total.

sentences.zh: 又三日益一，盡百三十日，率百八十四日行百六度。

translations.literal: Again every three days increase by one, exhaust one hundred thirty days, rate one hundred eighty-four days motion one hundred six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 every 3 days for 130 days, yielding 106 degrees in 184 days.

sentences.zh: 又二日益一，盡百四十四日，率百九十一日行百一十三度。

translations.literal: Again every two days increase by one, exhaust one hundred forty-four days, rate one hundred ninety-one days motion one hundred thirteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Next, increase by 1 every 2 days for 144 days, giving 113 degrees in 191 days.

sentences.zh: 又每日益一，盡百九十日，率二百三十七日行百五十九度。

translations.literal: Again each day increase by one, exhaust one hundred ninety days, rate two hundred thirty-seven days motion one hundred fifty-nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 each day for 190 days, yielding 159 degrees in 237 days.

sentences.zh: 又每日益二，盡二百日，率二百五十七日行百七十九度。

translations.literal: Again each day increase by two, exhaust two hundred days, rate two hundred fifty-seven days motion one hundred seventy-nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Next, increase by 2 each day for 200 days, giving 179 degrees in 257 days.

sentences.zh: 又每日益一，盡二百一十日，率二百六十七日行百八十九度，畢二百五十九日。

translations.literal: Again each day increase by one, exhaust two hundred ten days, rate two hundred sixty-seven days motion one hundred eighty-nine degrees, exhaust two hundred fifty-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Then increase by 1 each day for 210 days, yielding 189 degrees in 267 days—a segment totaling 259 days.

sentences.zh: 乃二日損一，畢大雪，復初。

translations.literal: Then every two days diminish by one, exhaust Great Snow, return to initial.
translations.idiomatic: Then decrease by 1 every 2 days until Great Snow, returning to the initial rate.

sentences.zh: 後遲加六度者，此後疾去度率六，為定。

translations.literal: If later slow added six degrees, this later rapid remove six from degree-rate, as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: If the later slow phase added 6 degrees, subtract 6 from the degree-rate in this later rapid phase—that is the fixed amount.

sentences.zh: 各依冬至後日數而損益之，為後疾日度率。

translations.literal: Each according to days after winter solstice increase or decrease them, as later rapid day-degree rates.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust each according to days past the winter solstice to obtain the later rapid day-rate and degree-rate.

sentences.zh: 若入立夏，畢夏至，日行半度，盡六十日，行三十度。

translations.literal: If entering Start of Summer through summer solstice, daily motion half a degree, exhaust sixty days, motion thirty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If entering between Start of Summer and summer solstice, move half a degree per day for 60 days, covering 30 degrees.

sentences.zh: 若入小暑，畢大暑，盡四十日，行二十度皆去日度率，別為半度之。

translations.literal: If entering Lesser Heat through Greater Heat, exhaust forty days, motion twenty degrees—all remove from day-degree rates, separately treat as half-degree motion.
translations.idiomatic: If entering between Lesser Heat and Greater Heat, for 40 days covering 20 degrees—set these aside from the day- and degree-rates as a separate half-degree segment.

sentences.zh: 行訖，然後求平行分，續之。

translations.literal: When motion is finished, then seek the uniform-motion parts and continue.
translations.idiomatic: When that segment is complete, calculate the uniform-motion parts and continue from there.

sentences.zh: 各盡其日度而伏。

translations.literal: Each exhausts its days and degrees then hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Continue until its allotted days and degrees are used up, then it disappears (conjunction).

sentences.zh: 率三百五十七萬八千二百四十六。

translations.literal: Rate three million five hundred seventy-eight thousand two hundred forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Circulation rate: 3,578,246.

sentences.zh: 終日三百七十八，行分六十一。

translations.literal: Total days three hundred seventy-eight, motion-parts sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Total days: 378; motion-parts: 61.

sentences.zh: 平見，入冬至初日，減四千八百一十四分。

translations.literal: Mean appearance, entering winter solstice first day, subtract four thousand eight hundred fourteen parts.
translations.idiomatic: For mean appearance, on the first day of winter solstice subtract 4,814 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃日增所減七十九分。

translations.literal: Then each day increase what was subtracted by seventy-nine parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then each day add back 79 parts of what was subtracted.

sentences.zh: 入小寒，均減九日。

translations.literal: Entering Lesser Cold, evenly subtract nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Lesser Cold, subtract an even 9 days.

sentences.zh: 乃每氣損所減一日。

translations.literal: Then each qi diminish what was subtracted by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Then reduce the subtraction by 1 day per solar term.

sentences.zh: 入夏至初日，均減二日。

translations.literal: Entering summer solstice first day, evenly subtract two days.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of summer solstice, subtract an even 2 days.

sentences.zh: 自後十日損所減一日。

translations.literal: From then every ten days diminish what was subtracted by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, reduce the subtraction by 1 day every 10 days.

sentences.zh: 小暑五日外，依平。

translations.literal: Lesser Heat beyond five days, follow the mean.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth day of Lesser Heat, use the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 入大暑，日增所加百八十一分。

translations.literal: Entering Greater Heat, each day increase what was added by one hundred eighty-one parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Greater Heat, each day add 181 parts to the increment.

sentences.zh: 入處暑，均加九日。

translations.literal: Entering End Heat, evenly add nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Entering End Heat, add an even 9 days.

sentences.zh: 入白露初日，加六千二分。

translations.literal: Entering White Dew first day, add six thousand two parts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of White Dew, add 6,002 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃日損所加百三十三分。

translations.literal: Then each day diminish what was added by one hundred thirty-three parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then each day reduce the increment by 133 parts.

sentences.zh: 入霜降，日增所減七十九分。

translations.literal: Entering Frost's Descent, each day increase what was subtracted by seventy-nine parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Frost's Descent, each day add back 79 parts of what was subtracted.

sentences.zh: 初見，順，日行六十分，八十三日行七度二百四十八分。

translations.literal: First appearance, direct, daily motion sixty parts, in eighty-three days motion seven degrees two hundred forty-eight parts.
translations.idiomatic: At first appearance, in direct motion at 60 parts per day, covering 7 degrees 248 parts in 83 days.

sentences.zh: 而留，三十八日。

translations.literal: Then stationary, thirty-eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Then stationary for 38 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退，日四十一分，百日退六度四十四分。

translations.literal: Then retrograde, daily forty-one parts, in one hundred days retrograde six degrees forty-four parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then retrograde at 41 parts per day, covering 6 degrees 44 parts in 100 days.

sentences.zh: 又留，三十七日六十一分。

translations.literal: Again stationary, thirty-seven days sixty-one parts.
translations.idiomatic: Stands still again for 37 days 61 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃順，日行六十分，八十三日行七度二百四十八分而伏。

translations.literal: Then direct, daily motion sixty parts, in eighty-three days motion seven degrees two hundred forty-eight parts then hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Then direct motion at 60 parts per day, 7 degrees 248 parts in 83 days, then disappears.

sentences.zh: 率五百五十二萬六千二百。

translations.literal: Rate five million five hundred twenty-six thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Circulation rate: 5,526,200.

sentences.zh: 終日五百八十三，行分六百二十，小分八。

translations.literal: Total days five hundred eighty-three, motion-parts six hundred twenty, minor parts eight.
translations.idiomatic: Total days: 583; motion-parts: 620; minor parts: 8.

sentences.zh: 晨見伏三百二十七日，行分六百二十，小分八。

translations.literal: Morning appearance-hidden three hundred twenty-seven days, motion-parts six hundred twenty, minor parts eight.
translations.idiomatic: Morning visibility and invisibility: 327 days; motion-parts: 620; minor parts: 8.

sentences.zh: 夕見伏二百五十六日。

translations.literal: Evening appearance-hidden two hundred fifty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Evening visibility and invisibility: 256 days.

sentences.zh: 晨平見，入冬至，依平。

translations.literal: Morning mean appearance, entering winter solstice, follow the mean.
translations.idiomatic: For morning mean appearance at winter solstice, use the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 入小寒，日增所加六十六分。

translations.literal: Entering Lesser Cold, each day increase what was added by sixty-six parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Lesser Cold, each day add 66 parts to the increment.

sentences.zh: 入立春，畢立夏，均加三日。

translations.literal: Entering Start of Spring through Start of Summer, evenly add three days.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Start of Spring through Start of Summer, add an even 3 days.

sentences.zh: 小滿初日，加千九百六十四分。

translations.literal: Lesser Full Grain first day, add one thousand nine hundred sixty-four parts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of Lesser Full Grain, add 1,964 parts.

sentences.zh: 乃日損所加六十分。

translations.literal: Then each day diminish what was added by sixty parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then each day reduce the increment by 60 parts.

sentences.zh: 入夏至，依平。

translations.literal: Entering summer solstice, follow the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Entering summer solstice, use the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 入小暑，日增所減六十分。

translations.literal: Entering Lesser Heat, each day increase what was subtracted by sixty parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Lesser Heat, each day add back 60 parts of what was subtracted.

sentences.zh: 入立秋，畢立冬，均減三日。

sentences.zh: 交會法千二百七十四萬一千二百五八分。

translations.literal: Conjunction divisor twelve million seven hundred forty-one thousand two hundred fifty-eight parts.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction divisor: 12,741,258 parts.

sentences.zh: 交分法六百三十七萬六百二九分。

translations.literal: Node-parts factor six million three hundred seventy thousand six hundred twenty-nine parts.
translations.idiomatic: Node-parts factor: 6,370,629 parts.

sentences.zh: 朔差百八萬五千四百九十四二分。

translations.literal: New-moon difference one million eighty-five thousand four hundred ninety-four parts.
translations.idiomatic: New-moon difference: 1,085,494 parts.

sentences.zh: 望分六百九十一萬三千三百五十。

translations.literal: Full-moon parts six million nine hundred thirteen thousand three hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Full-moon parts: 6,913,350.

sentences.zh: 交限五百八十二萬七千八百五十五八分。

translations.literal: Conjunction limit five million eight hundred twenty-seven thousand eight hundred fifty-five parts.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction limit: 5,827,855 parts.

sentences.zh: 望差五十四萬二千七百四十七一分。

translations.literal: Full-moon difference five hundred forty-two thousand seven hundred forty-seven parts.
translations.idiomatic: Full-moon difference: 542,747 parts.

sentences.zh: 外限六百七十六萬七百八十二九分。

translations.literal: Outer limit six million seven hundred sixty thousand seven hundred eighty-two parts.
translations.idiomatic: Outer limit: 6,760,782 parts.

sentences.zh: 中限千二百三十五萬一千二十五八分。

translations.literal: Middle limit twelve million three hundred fifty-one thousand twenty-five parts.
translations.idiomatic: Middle limit: 12,351,025 parts.

sentences.zh: 內限千二百一十九萬一千四百五十八七分。

translations.literal: Inner limit twelve million one hundred ninety-one thousand four hundred fifty-eight parts.
translations.idiomatic: Inner limit: 12,191,458 parts.

sentences.zh: 以朔差乘積月，滿交會法去之；

translations.literal: Use new-moon difference multiply accumulated months, full conjunction divisor remove it;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated months by the new-moon difference and discard full multiples of the conjunction divisor;

sentences.zh: 餘得天正月朔入平交分。

translations.literal: Remainder obtains first month of heaven new moon entering mean node parts.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder is the mean node parts at the first month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 求望，以望分加之。

translations.literal: Seek full moon, use full-moon parts to add it.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon, add the full-moon parts.

sentences.zh: 求次月，以朔差加之。

translations.literal: Seek next month, use new-moon difference to add it.
translations.idiomatic: For the next month, add the new-moon difference.

sentences.zh: 其朔望，入大雪，畢冬至，依平。

translations.literal: Its new and full moons, entering Great Snow through winter solstice, follow the mean.
translations.idiomatic: For new and full moons entering Great Snow through winter solstice, use the mean node parts.

sentences.zh: 入小寒，日加氣差千六百五十分。

translations.literal: Entering Lesser Cold, each day add qi-difference one thousand six hundred fifty parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Lesser Cold, add 1,650 parts of qi-difference each day.

sentences.zh: 入啟蟄，畢清明，均加七萬六千一百分。

translations.literal: Entering Awakening of Insects through Clear and Bright, evenly add seventy-six thousand one hundred parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Awakening of Insects through Clear and Bright, add an even 76,100 parts.

sentences.zh: 自後日損所加千六百五十分。

translations.literal: From then each day diminish what was added by one thousand six hundred fifty parts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, reduce the increment by 1,650 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 入芒種，畢夏至，依平。

translations.literal: Entering Grain in Ear through summer solstice, follow the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Grain in Ear through summer solstice, use the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 加之滿法，去之。

translations.literal: Adding it when full of factor, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: When the sum fills the divisor, discard the full amount.

sentences.zh: 若朔交入小寒畢雨水，及立夏畢小滿，值盈二時已下，皆半氣差加之。

translations.literal: If new-moon node enters Lesser Cold through Rain Water, and Start of Summer through Lesser Full Grain, meeting waxing two double-hours and below, all half qi-difference add it.
translations.idiomatic: If the new-moon node falls between Lesser Cold and Rain Water, or Start of Summer and Lesser Full Grain, and the moon is waxing through the second double-hour or earlier, add half the qi-difference.

sentences.zh: 二時已上則否。

translations.literal: Two double-hours and above then not.
translations.idiomatic: At the second double-hour or later, do not.

sentences.zh: 如望差已下、外限已上有星伏，木、土去見十日外，火去見四十日外，金晨伏去見二十二日外，有一星者，不加氣差。

translations.literal: If below full-moon difference and above outer limit a star is hidden—Wood and Earth beyond ten days from appearance, Fire beyond forty days from appearance, Venus morning hidden beyond twenty-two days from appearance, having one star—do not add qi-difference.
translations.idiomatic: If below the full-moon difference and above the outer limit a planet is invisible—Jupiter or Saturn more than 10 days from appearance, Mars more than 40 days, Venus morning invisibility more than 22 days—and one such planet is present, do not add the qi-difference.

sentences.zh: 入小暑後，日增所減千二百分。

translations.literal: After Lesser Heat, each day increase what was subtracted by one thousand two hundred parts.
translations.idiomatic: After Lesser Heat, each day add back 1,200 parts of what was subtracted.

sentences.zh: 入白露，畢霜降，均減九萬五千八百二十五分。

translations.literal: Entering White Dew through Frost's Descent, evenly subtract ninety-five thousand eight hundred twenty-five parts.
translations.idiomatic: Entering White Dew through Frost's Descent, subtract an even 95,825 parts.

sentences.zh: 立冬初日，減六萬三千三百分，自後日損所減二千一百一十分。

translations.literal: Start of Winter first day, subtract sixty-three thousand three hundred parts, from then each day diminish what was subtracted by two thousand one hundred ten parts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of Start of Winter, subtract 63,300 parts; thereafter reduce the subtraction by 2,110 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 減若不足，加法，乃減之，餘為定交分。

translations.literal: If subtraction insufficient, add the factor, then subtract it, remainder as fixed node parts.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction would go negative, add the divisor and then subtract—the remainder is the fixed node parts.

sentences.zh: 朔入交分，如交限內限已上、交分中限已下有星伏如前者，不減。

translations.literal: New moon entering node parts, if like conjunction limit inner limit and above, node-parts middle limit and below a star hidden as before, do not subtract.
translations.idiomatic: If at new moon the node parts are above the inner limit of the conjunction limit and below the middle limit, and a planet is invisible as described above, do not subtract.

sentences.zh: 不滿交分法者，為在外道；

translations.literal: If not full of node-parts factor, is on outer path;
translations.idiomatic: If less than the node-parts factor, the moon is on the outer path;

sentences.zh: 滿去之，餘為在內道。

translations.literal: Full then remove it, remainder is on inner path.
translations.idiomatic: If full, discard the factor; the remainder means the inner path.

sentences.zh: 如望差已下，為去先交分，交限已上，以減交分，餘為去後交分。

translations.literal: If below full-moon difference, is distance from prior node parts; conjunction limit and above, use to subtract node parts, remainder is distance from subsequent node parts.
translations.idiomatic: If below the full-moon difference, this is the distance from the prior node; at the conjunction limit and above, subtract from the node parts—the remainder is the distance from the subsequent node.

sentences.zh: 皆三日法約，為時數。

translations.literal: All use three time-factor to reduce, as double-hour count.
translations.idiomatic: Divide all by 3 and then by the time-factor to get the double-hour count.

sentences.zh: 望則月蝕，朔在內道則日蝕。

translations.literal: Full moon then lunar eclipse, new moon on inner path then solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At full moon there is a lunar eclipse; at new moon on the inner path there is a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 雖在外道，去交近，亦蝕。

translations.literal: Although on outer path, if near node, also eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the outer path, if close to the node, there is still an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 在內道，去交遠，亦不蝕。

translations.literal: On inner path, if far from node, also no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the inner path, if far from the node, there is no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 置蝕望定小餘。

translations.literal: Set eclipse full-moon fixed minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside the fixed minor remainder for the eclipse full moon.

sentences.zh: 入曆一日，減二百八十；

translations.literal: Enter sequence one day, subtract two hundred eighty;
translations.idiomatic: On sequence day 1, subtract 280;

sentences.zh: 若十五日，即加之；

translations.literal: If fifteenth day, then add it;
translations.idiomatic: On day 15, add instead;

sentences.zh: 十四日，加五百五十；

translations.literal: Fourteenth day, add five hundred fifty;
translations.idiomatic: On day 14, add 550;

sentences.zh: 若二十八日，即減之；

translations.literal: If twenty-eighth day, then subtract it;
translations.idiomatic: On day 28, subtract instead;

sentences.zh: 餘日皆盈加、縮減二百八十：為月蝕定餘。

translations.literal: Remaining days all waxing add, waning subtract two hundred eighty: as lunar eclipse fixed remainder.
translations.idiomatic: On all other days, add 280 when waxing and subtract 280 when waning—this is the fixed remainder for lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十二乘之，時法而一，命子半算外；

translations.literal: Twelve multiply it, time-factor divide as one, count from midnight of zi beyond;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 12, divide by the time-factor, and count from midnight of zi;

sentences.zh: 不盡，得月蝕加時。

translations.literal: Not exhausted, obtain lunar eclipse add-time.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder gives the lunar eclipse time.

sentences.zh: 約定小餘如夜漏半已下者，退日算上。

translations.literal: Reduce fixed minor remainder if below half of night clepsydra, retreat one on day count.
translations.idiomatic: If the fixed minor remainder is below half the night's clepsydra outflow, move back one day on the day count.

sentences.zh: 置蝕朔定小餘。

translations.literal: Set eclipse new-moon fixed minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside the fixed minor remainder for the eclipse new moon.

sentences.zh: 入曆一日，即減二百八十；

translations.literal: Enter sequence one day, then subtract two hundred eighty;
translations.idiomatic: On sequence day 1, subtract 280;

sentences.zh: 若十五日，即加之；

translations.literal: If fifteenth day, then add it;
translations.idiomatic: On day 15, add instead;

sentences.zh: 十四日，加五百五十；

translations.literal: Fourteenth day, add five hundred fifty;
translations.idiomatic: On day 14, add 550;

sentences.zh: 若二十八日，即減之；

translations.literal: If twenty-eighth day, then subtract it;
translations.idiomatic: On day 28, subtract instead;

sentences.zh: 為定。

translations.literal: As fixed.
translations.idiomatic: This gives the fixed value.

sentences.zh: 後不入四時加減之限。

translations.literal: Afterward do not enter the four-seasons add-subtract limit.
translations.idiomatic: After this, do not apply the four-seasons add-subtract limits.

sentences.zh: 其內道，春，去交四時已上入曆，盈加、縮減二百八十；

translations.literal: If inner path, spring, distance from node four double-hours and above enter sequence, waxing add waning subtract two hundred eighty;
translations.idiomatic: On the inner path in spring, if the node distance is 4 double-hours or more and the sequence is entered, add 280 when waxing and subtract when waning;

sentences.zh: 夏，盈加、縮減二百八十；

translations.literal: Summer, waxing add waning subtract two hundred eighty;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, add 280 when waxing and subtract when waning;

sentences.zh: 秋，去交十一時已下，惟盈加二百八十，已上者，盈加五百五十，縮加二百八十；

translations.literal: Autumn, distance from node eleven double-hours and below, only waxing add two hundred eighty, if above, waxing add five hundred fifty, waning add two hundred eighty;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, if node distance is 11 double-hours or below, add only 280 when waxing; if above, add 550 when waxing and add 280 when waning;

sentences.zh: 冬，去交五時已下，惟盈加二百八十：皆為定餘。

translations.literal: Winter, distance from node five double-hours and below, only waxing add two hundred eighty: all as fixed remainder.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, if node distance is 5 double-hours or below, add only 280 when waxing—all as the fixed remainder.

sentences.zh: 十二乘之，時法而一，命子半算外；

translations.literal: Twelve multiply it, time-factor divide as one, count from midnight of zi beyond;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 12, divide by the time-factor, and count from midnight of zi;

sentences.zh: 不盡，為時餘，副之。

translations.literal: Not exhausted, as time remainder, set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder is the time remainder—set it aside.

sentences.zh: 仲辰半前，以副減法為差率；

translations.literal: First double-hour before half, use aside to subtract factor as difference-rate;
translations.idiomatic: In the first double-hour before the half-period, subtract the aside from the factor to get the difference-rate;

sentences.zh: 半後，退半辰，以法加餘，以副為差率。

translations.literal: After half, retreat half double-hour, use factor add remainder, use aside as difference-rate.
translations.idiomatic: After the half-period, retreat half a double-hour, add the remainder to the factor, and use the aside as the difference-rate.

sentences.zh: 季辰半前，以法加副為差率；

translations.literal: Intermediate double-hour before half, use factor add aside as difference-rate;
translations.idiomatic: In the intermediate double-hour before the half-period, add the aside to the factor for the difference-rate;

sentences.zh: 半後，退半辰，以法加餘，倍法加副，為差率。

translations.literal: After half, retreat half double-hour, use factor add remainder, double factor add aside, as difference-rate.
translations.idiomatic: After the half-period, retreat half a double-hour, add the remainder to the factor, double the factor and add the aside—that is the difference-rate.

sentences.zh: 孟辰半前，三因其法，以副減之，餘為差率；

translations.literal: First double-hour before half, thrice multiply its factor, use aside to subtract it, remainder as difference-rate;
translations.idiomatic: In the first double-hour before the half-period, triple the factor, subtract the aside—the remainder is the difference-rate;

sentences.zh: 半後，退半辰，以法加餘，又以法加副，乃三因其法，以副減之，為差率。

translations.literal: After half, retreat half double-hour, use factor add remainder, again use factor add aside, then thrice multiply its factor, use aside to subtract it, as difference-rate.
translations.idiomatic: After the half-period, retreat half a double-hour, add the remainder to the factor, add the aside to the factor, then triple the factor and subtract the aside—that is the difference-rate.

sentences.zh: 又置去交時數，三已下，加三；

translations.literal: Also set distance-from-node double-hour count, three and below, add three;
translations.idiomatic: Also set the node-distance in double-hours: if 3 or below, add 3;

sentences.zh: 六已下，加二；

translations.literal: Six and below, add two;
translations.idiomatic: if 6 or below, add 2;

sentences.zh: 九已下，加一；

translations.literal: Nine and below, add one;
translations.idiomatic: if 9 or below, add 1;

sentences.zh: 九已上，依數；

translations.literal: Nine and above, follow the number;
translations.idiomatic: if above 9, use the number as is;

sentences.zh: 十二已上，從十二。

translations.literal: Twelve and above, follow twelve.
translations.idiomatic: if 12 or above, cap at 12.

sentences.zh: 若季辰半後，孟辰半前，去交六時已上者，皆從其六。

translations.literal: If intermediate double-hour after half, first double-hour before half, distance from node six double-hours and above, all follow its six.
translations.idiomatic: If in the intermediate double-hour after the half-period or the first double-hour before the half-period the node distance is 6 double-hours or more, use 6 in all cases.

sentences.zh: 六時已下，依數不加。

translations.literal: Six double-hours and below, follow the number without adding.
translations.idiomatic: At 6 double-hours or below, use the number without adding.

sentences.zh: 皆乘差率，十四除，為時差。

translations.literal: All multiply difference-rate, fourteen divide, as time-difference.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply all by the difference-rate and divide by 14 to get the time-difference.

sentences.zh: 子午半後，以加時餘；

translations.literal: Zi-wu after half, use to add time remainder;
translations.idiomatic: After the half-period of zi and wu, add to the time remainder;

sentences.zh: 卯酉半後，以減時餘；

translations.literal: Mao-you after half, use to subtract time remainder;
translations.idiomatic: After the half-period of mao and you, subtract from the time remainder;

sentences.zh: 加之滿若不足，進退時法：孟謂寅、巳、申，仲謂午、卯、酉，季謂辰、未、戌。

translations.literal: Adding when full or insufficient, advance retreat time-factor: first means yin, si, shen; intermediate means wu, mao, you; last means chen, wei, xu.
translations.idiomatic: When addition overflows or subtraction underflows, adjust by the time-factor: first double-hours are yin, si, shen; intermediate are wu, mao, you; last are chen, wei, xu.

sentences.zh: 得日蝕加時。

translations.literal: Obtain solar eclipse add-time.
translations.idiomatic: This yields the solar eclipse time.

sentences.zh: 望去交分，冬先後交，皆去二時；

translations.literal: Remove distance-from-node parts, winter prior and subsequent node, all remove two double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: For node distance: in winter, whether before or after the node, subtract 2 double-hours;

sentences.zh: 春先交，秋後交，去半時；

translations.literal: Spring prior node, autumn subsequent node, remove half double-hour;
translations.idiomatic: in spring before the node and autumn after the node, subtract half a double-hour;

sentences.zh: 春後交，秋先交，去二時；

translations.literal: Spring subsequent node, autumn prior node, remove two double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: in spring after the node and autumn before the node, subtract 2 double-hours;

sentences.zh: 夏則依定。

translations.literal: Summer then follow fixed.
translations.idiomatic: in summer, use the fixed value.

sentences.zh: 不足去者，既。

translations.literal: If insufficient to remove, total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction would go negative, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 乃以三萬六千一百八十三為法而一，以減十五，餘為月蝕分。

translations.literal: Then use thirty-six thousand one hundred eighty-three as factor divide as one, subtract from fifteen, remainder as lunar eclipse parts.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 36,183; subtract the quotient from 15—the remainder is the lunar eclipse magnitude.

sentences.zh: 朔去交，在內道，五月朔，加時在南方，先交十三時外；

translations.literal: New moon distance from node, on inner path, fifth-month new moon, add-time in south, prior node beyond thirteen double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: For new-moon node distance on the inner path: on a fifth-month new moon with eclipse time in the south and prior node beyond 13 double-hours;

sentences.zh: 六月朔，後交十三時外者，不蝕。

translations.literal: Sixth-month new moon, subsequent node beyond thirteen double-hours, no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: on a sixth-month new moon with subsequent node beyond 13 double-hours—no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 啟蟄畢清明，先交十三時外，值縮，加時在未西；

translations.literal: Awakening of Insects through Clear and Bright, prior node beyond thirteen double-hours, meeting waning, add-time in wei west;
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of Insects through Clear and Bright, prior node beyond 13 double-hours, moon waning, eclipse time in wei west;

sentences.zh: 處暑畢寒露，後交十三時外，值盈，加時在巳東，皆不蝕。

translations.literal: End Heat through Cold Dew, subsequent node beyond thirteen double-hours, meeting waxing, add-time in si east, all no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: End Heat through Cold Dew, subsequent node beyond 13 double-hours, moon waxing, eclipse time in si east—in all cases, no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 交在外道，先後去交一時內者，皆蝕。

translations.literal: Node on outer path, prior and subsequent distance from node within one double-hour, all eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If the node is on the outer path and the distance before or after the node is within 1 double-hour, there is an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 若二時內，及先交值盈、後交值縮二時外者，亦蝕。

translations.literal: If within two double-hours, and prior node meeting waxing, subsequent node meeting waning beyond two double-hours, also eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If within 2 double-hours, or prior node with waxing moon or subsequent node with waning moon beyond 2 double-hours, there is also an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏去交二時內，加時在南方者，亦蝕。

translations.literal: Summer within two double-hours from node, add-time in south, also eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, within 2 double-hours of the node with eclipse time in the south, there is also an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 若去分、至十二時內，去交六時內者，亦蝕。

translations.literal: If within twelve double-hours from equinox or solstice, within six double-hours from node, also eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If within 12 double-hours of an equinox or solstice and within 6 double-hours of the node, there is also an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 若去春分三日內，後交二時；

translations.literal: If within three days from spring equinox, subsequent node two double-hours;
translations.idiomatic: If within 3 days of the spring equinox and subsequent node within 2 double-hours;

sentences.zh: 秋分三日內，先交二時內者，亦蝕。

translations.literal: Within three days from autumn equinox, prior node within two double-hours, also eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: or within 3 days of the autumn equinox and prior node within 2 double-hours, there is also an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 諸去交三時內有星伏，土、木去見十日外，火去見四十日外，金晨伏去見二十二日外，有一星者，不蝕。

translations.literal: All within three double-hours from node having star hidden—Earth and Wood beyond ten days from appearance, Fire beyond forty days from appearance, Venus morning hidden beyond twenty-two days from appearance, having one star—no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If within 3 double-hours of the node a planet is invisible—Saturn or Jupiter more than 10 days from appearance, Mars more than 40 days, Venus morning invisibility more than 22 days—and one such planet is present, no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 各置去交分。

translations.literal: Each set distance-from-node parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the distance-from-node parts for each case.

sentences.zh: 秋分後，畢立春，均減二十二萬八百分。

translations.literal: After autumn equinox through Start of Spring, evenly subtract two hundred twenty-eight thousand eight hundred parts.
translations.idiomatic: After the autumn equinox through Start of Spring, subtract an even 228,800 parts.

sentences.zh: 啟蟄初日，畢芒種，日損所減千八百一十分。

translations.literal: Awakening of Insects first day through Grain in Ear, each day diminish what was subtracted by one thousand eight hundred ten parts.
translations.idiomatic: From the first day of Awakening of Insects through Grain in Ear, reduce the subtraction by 1,810 parts each day.

sentences.zh: 夏至後，畢白露，日增所減二千四百分。

translations.literal: After summer solstice through White Dew, each day increase what was subtracted by two thousand four hundred parts.
translations.idiomatic: After summer solstice through White Dew, add back 2,400 parts of the subtraction each day.

sentences.zh: 以減去交分，餘為不蝕分。

translations.literal: Use to subtract distance-from-node parts, remainder as non-eclipse parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract this from the distance-from-node parts—the remainder is the non-eclipse threshold.

sentences.zh: 不足減，反相減為不蝕分。

translations.literal: If insufficient to subtract, inversely subtract as non-eclipse parts.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction would go negative, reverse the subtraction to get the non-eclipse threshold.

sentences.zh: 亦以減望差為定法。

translations.literal: Also use to subtract full-moon difference as fixed divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Also subtract this from the full-moon difference to get the fixed divisor.

sentences.zh: 後交值縮者，直以望差為定法。

translations.literal: If subsequent node meets waning, directly use full-moon difference as fixed divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If the subsequent node occurs during waning, use the full-moon difference directly as the fixed divisor.

sentences.zh: 其不蝕分，大寒畢立春，後交五時外，皆去一時。

translations.literal: Its non-eclipse parts, Great Cold through Start of Spring, subsequent node beyond five double-hours, all remove one double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: For the non-eclipse threshold: Great Cold through Start of Spring, subsequent node beyond 5 double-hours—subtract 1 double-hour in all cases.

sentences.zh: 時差值減者，先交減之，後交加之。

translations.literal: If time-difference value subtract, prior node subtract it, subsequent node add it.
translations.idiomatic: If the time-difference calls for subtraction, subtract for the prior node and add for the subsequent node.

sentences.zh: 時差值加者，先交加之，後交減之。

translations.literal: If time-difference value add, prior node add it, subsequent node subtract it.
translations.idiomatic: If the time-difference calls for addition, add for the prior node and subtract for the subsequent node.

sentences.zh: 不足減者，皆既。

translations.literal: If insufficient to subtract, all total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction would go negative, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 十五乘之，定法而一，以減十五，餘為日蝕分。

translations.literal: Fifteen multiply it, fixed divisor divide as one, subtract from fifteen, remainder as solar eclipse parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 15, divide by the fixed divisor, subtract the quotient from 15—the remainder is the solar eclipse magnitude.

sentences.zh: 置日月蝕分，四已下，因增二；

translations.literal: Set sun and moon eclipse parts, four and below, accordingly increase two;
translations.idiomatic: For eclipse magnitude: if 4 or below, add 2;

sentences.zh: 五已下，因增三；

translations.literal: Five and below, accordingly increase three;
translations.idiomatic: if 5 or below, add 3;

sentences.zh: 六已上，因增五；

translations.literal: Six and above, accordingly increase five;
translations.idiomatic: if 6 or above, add 5;

sentences.zh: 各為刻率，副之。

translations.literal: Each as quarter-rate, set aside.
translations.idiomatic: each becomes the quarter-rate—set it aside.

sentences.zh: 以乘所入曆損益率，四千五十七為法而一。

translations.literal: Use to multiply entered sequence increase-decrease rate, four thousand fifty-seven as factor divide as one.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the sequence increase-decrease rate and divide by 4,057.

sentences.zh: 值盈，反其損益；

translations.literal: Meeting waxing, reverse its increase-decrease;
translations.idiomatic: If waxing, reverse the increase-decrease;

sentences.zh: 值縮，依其損益。

translations.literal: Meeting waning, follow its increase-decrease.
translations.idiomatic: If waning, follow the increase-decrease.

sentences.zh: 皆損益其副，為定用刻。

translations.literal: All increase-decrease its aside, as fixed usable quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the increase-decrease to the aside value—this is the fixed usable quarter-count.

sentences.zh: 乃六乘之，十而一，以減蝕甚辰刻，為虧初。

translations.literal: Then six multiply it, ten divide as one, subtract from eclipse maximum double-hour quarters, as beginning of obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 6, divide by 10, subtract from the maximum-eclipse double-hour quarters—this is the beginning of obscuration.

sentences.zh: 又四乘之，十而一。

translations.literal: Again four multiply it, ten divide as one.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 4 and divide by 10 again.

sentences.zh: 以加食甚辰刻，為復滿。

translations.literal: Use to add maximum-eclipse double-hour quarters, as full restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Add to the maximum-eclipse double-hour quarters—this is full restoration.
